newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela's Sivensa sees rising exports for 97.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela's Sivensa sees rising exports for 97.

text.p: Leading Venezuelan steel firm Sivensa expects to gently increase exports in the coming year, while rising Venezuelan car production should also boost domestic demand, company president Henrique Machado Zuloaga said.
"We expect exports to improve, even if only moderately, to between some $300 and $350 million," Machado told reporters.
Exports in fiscal year 1996 reached $315 million, accounting for nearly half of total company sales. Among domestic markets, Machado said the company had seen rising car part sales in January.

The company's $756 million investment program for the year will be part financed by loans and partly from the recent issue of $180 million of Class B shares, Machado added. The investments will be largely used to boost car parts, including wire and iron briquette production, he said.

Sivensa's first quarter net profits rose to 1.788 billion bolivars, compared with 1.098 billion in the same period the year before, on sales of 74.1 billion bolivars versus 60.8 billion bolivars in the first quarter of fiscal 1996.
